scope: Read-only source/config/saved-receipt audit; wrote only these two sibling audit files. No network, UI, tests, deployment or repository edits.

historicalMonitorMetadata.provenance: Earlier approved Wrangler deployments status and versions view tool receipts in this task, not refreshed by this audit.

routes.exposes: Actual next alarm time, latest global scheduler tick, public configuration/coverage limits; no user ID or table counts.
routes.limit: A global tick does not prove each owner job ran. Held code returns503 before Auth and before this GET body.

routes.exposes: Current verified owner nonarchived jobs: IDs, kind, supplied params, enabled state, interval, next due, prior check/change, coverage and per-job allowance.
routes.limit: At most100; no archived jobs, token hashes, revision or raw leases; publicJob omits ownerUUID.

routes.exposes: Same current-owner job detail and coverage.
routes.limit: Unknown/foreign/archived job returns404; does not enumerate other users.

routes.exposes: Owner-scoped bounded check history, source snapshots/failure receipts, hashes, latest retained verified snapshot and comparison policy. History rows include ownerUUID.
routes.limit: 1-100 rows, not a complete export; latest_verified may be older than returned history window.

routes.exposes: Owner alerts with retained evidence and actual stored/received/read status; optional unread=true.
routes.limit: Latest100 only; no acknowledgment mutation needed for comparison.

routes.exposes: Owner feed IDs, labels, enabled state, last observation/receipt and creation times.
routes.limit: Deliberately excludes tokens and token hashes.

routes.exposes: Owner rule IDs, ownerUUID/feed link, enabled state, polygon/rule state and observed timestamps.
routes.limit: Private source data must stay private; no whole-namespace export.

routes.exposes: Remote verified accountUUID used for every monitor owner filter.
routes.limit: Call each source/target only with its actual current session and public key; never print or copy bearer tokens into audit.

routes.exposes: Existing target account-plan and explicit tool-denial checks used before create/resume/manual execution.
routes.limit: Monitor read GETs do not themselves certify these entitlements; no service-role credential is needed.

heldReadLimitation.detail: migrationSession precedes Auth and all monitorGETs. Known hold gives503 code migration_hold; no user session is required to observe that code, but a trusted bound route is required. It does not disclose generation/jobcounts/exact alarm state. Initialization failures may disclose alarm-disarm verification via header; normal hold does not expose this header.

releaseGates: Actual target preview sign-in and correct original ownerUUID.
Verified existing namespace/service identity and precise reversible config delta.
Instrumented hold response and reconciliation of preexisting uninstrumented operations.
Before/after owner-scoped record/access comparison and target entitlement checks before resuming existing approved monitoring.
optionalHardeningNotBlanketBlockers: A complete monitor namespace export or token-hash dump is not required for an Auth URL/public-key change that keeps the same namespace and performs no data transformation.

A fresh complete storage backup is prudent but no specific irreversible data-loss action exists in this bounded same-namespace Auth rebind. Do not manufacture a new approval/access gate solely to add one.
Existing GETs intentionally do not expose all users, archived records, full histories, raw leases, generation or feed-token hashes. Their absence is not a reason to create an admin/export endpoint.
cutoverSteps: Complete actual independent-preview sign-in and verify the expected original accountUUID. This remains the main user-facing release gate; preserved databaseUUIDs alone do not prove a working session.

Before hold, capture a sanitized current-owner baseline through existing GET status/jobs/job/history/alerts/feeds/rules and independently verify the current userUUID. Record IDs/counts/hashes privately as appropriate; do not claim these bounded GETs are a complete namespace export.

Record current service/version/namespace/config identity through the established read-only deployment metadata route. Keep insight-nexus-monitors, MONITOR_STORE, MonitorStore and singleton scheduler unchanged. Do not create/delete/rename a namespace or perform a storage restore.

Roll out the already tested instrumented version with explicit hold. Verify a503 body with code migration_hold through the bound Worker route; a generic unbound Pages503 is insufficient. Reconcile older in-flight code because the first deployment cannot retroactively fence it. New instrumented operations cannot poll/mutate while held.

While held, update only the same Worker authentication URL/public key to ocliymtdvtxfxczxgbjr, retaining the hold, namespace and application data. Backend session/plan/permission GETs can be checked directly with the current target user session. All monitor GETs themselves return503 while held; do not claim they can inspect records or exact alarms in this state.

After verified identity/configuration, deliberately release with exact MONITOR_MIGRATION_HOLD=false and verify same-owner GET baseline parity plus actual status next_alarm_at/latest tick. Existing enabled jobs may resume their previously authorized polling immediately; this is not a provider-free validation window.

Confirm Pages uses MARKETPLACE_MONITOR bound to this same service and preserve APP_ORIGIN/feed ingress host as intended. Keep licensed bridge unconfigured. Record exact new version and rollback configuration without exposing key/token values.
rollbackChecks: Re-enter hold using the instrumented code, verify the distinct hold503, then restore previous Auth URL/public key if target sign-in or owner access fails. Keep the same namespace, class, singleton and retained control table.
Compare the same existing GET routes after deliberate release. Temporary sign-in failure from a wrong URL/key is reversible and does not itself delete monitor data.
Never use the old uninstrumented source version as a hold-preserving rollback: it ignores the persisted hold. Code rollback and storage rollback are different operations.

No table copy/drop, owner rewrite or storage restore is needed for this same-namespace Auth rebinding. If a later step would change namespace identity, rewrite userIDs, restore historical storage or delete data, a verified backup/recovery point becomes necessary before that separate operation.
Preserve/reconcile any application writes made before or after cutover. Already-dispatched external requests and pre-hold writes cannot be undone; do not silently reset storage to an older point.

savedOfflineEvidence.acceptance: Historical offline fixture result only; no live cutover acceptance.

remainingPrimaryStep: User completes independent preview sign-in; root already requested it. No production cutover was performed in this audit.
